manifest.name: dsh-skill-on-demand
manifest.description: Keeps the session skill catalog out of every request: skills are listed on demand, the ones a task needs are recorded once, and only a picked skill is loaded by name.

meta.title: Skill On Demand
meta.description: Lists skills on demand and keeps only the ones a task needs, instead of injecting the whole catalog into every request.

readme.text:
English | [中文](README.zh.md)

DeepSeek Harness injects every installed skill's full description into each request. With dozens of skills that is tens of thousands of tokens re-sent every turn, most of it about skills the task never touches. Removing the catalog outright saves the tokens but makes skills invisible: the model stops calling them.
This plugin lands in the middle: a **one-line index** of every skill (name + a short clause from its description), injected once per session, and full instructions loaded only on demand.

| Before | With this plugin |
| --- | --- |
| Full 500-char description per skill, re-sent every turn | One line per skill (`name: <28-char clause>`), once per session |
| Nothing searchable mid-session | `skill_list query=关键词` ranks the full descriptions and returns the closest matches |
| Nothing records what a task uses | `skill_pick` optionally records the chosen skills |
| Every body reachable but unmeasured | `skill` loads exactly one full body, by name |
The index is about a third of the full catalog, so the model can still read what each skill does; the expensive full descriptions and bodies stay out until needed.

readme.section: How the full catalog is removed
readme.text:
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-skill` publishes its catalog only while `ctx.tools.get('skill', agent)` resolves to its own tool registration. This plugin registers a same-name `skill` tool in each agent's own scope (the nearest scope wins), so that check fails and the catalog stops being published. The replacement tool does the same job — load one skill's instructions by exact name.

Presets that never mounted a `skill` tool are left untouched.

- A request that reads like browser work (网页 / 浏览器 / 抓取 / 登录 / screenshot / browser …) → name the `browser_*` tools (or `browser-skill` if the tools are absent).
- A `web_*` tool call fails → point at `browser_session` → `browser_page` → `browser_inspect`.
- Every message is matched against all skill descriptions locally (CJK bigrams + latin words, common phrases filtered); up to three matches are named with an 80-character description, once each per session.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-skill-on-demand
```

Restart the harness afterwards; the bundle is loaded at boot.
Start a new session and ask anything. The first turn should show the compact `<available_skills>` index, one line per skill, and `skill_list query=简历` should return `resume-builder`.

- The 28-character clause is a truncation, not a summary; a few skills need `skill_list query=` or `skill` to be understood.
- Selection via `skill_pick` is optional and per session.
- A session that already carried the full catalog still shows it, plus the shipped plugin's "no skills available" correction. Start a fresh session for a clean slate.
- If a preset registered `skill` in the agent's own layer, registration fails and the plugin degrades to "picker tools available, full catalog unchanged".

`index.js` is a single Host plugin, no build step. Run the self-check from inside the installed package, so module resolution reaches the harness's own `@deepseek-ai/*` packages:

```sh
node <profile>/node_modules/dsh-skill-on-demand/scripts/selftest.mjs
```
